verses.text: Remember, O Jehovah, what is come upon us: Behold, and see our reproach.

verses.text: Our inheritance is turned unto strangers, Our houses unto aliens.

verses.text: We are orphans and fatherless; Our mothers are as widows.

verses.text: We have drunken our water for money; Our wood is sold unto us.

verses.text: Our pursuers are upon our necks: We are weary, and have no rest.

verses.text: We have given the hand to the Egyptians, And to the Assyrians, to be satisfied with bread.

verses.text: Our fathers sinned, and are not; And we have borne their iniquities.

verses.text: Servants rule over us: There is none to deliver us out of their hand.

verses.text: We get our bread at the peril of our lives, Because of the sword of the wilderness.

verses.text: Our skin is black like an oven, Because of the burning heat of famine.

verses.text: They ravished the women in Zion, The virgins in the cities of Judah.

verses.text: Princes were hanged up by their hand: The faces of elders were not honored.

verses.text: The young men bare the mill; And the children stumbled under the wood.

verses.text: The elders have ceased from the gate, The young men from their music.

verses.text: The joy of our heart is ceased; Our dance is turned into mourning.

verses.text: The crown is fallen from our head: Woe unto us! for we have sinned.

verses.text: For this our heart is faint; For these things our eyes are dim;

verses.text: For the mountain of Zion, which is desolate: The foxes walk upon it.

verses.text: Thou, O Jehovah, abidest for ever; Thy throne is from generation to generation.

verses.text: Wherefore dost thou forget us for ever, And forsake us so long time?

verses.text: Turn thou us unto thee, O Jehovah, and we shall be turned; Renew our days as of old.
